metadata.title: How Ex-FBI Agents Skip Trace Anyone for Real Estate Deals
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
When you can't find an heir, the deal dies. Sean and Larry Baker are retired FBI agents turned private investigators, and they help real estate investors find the people nobody else can: heirs in prison, owners living overseas, people couch surfing with no phone in their name, and people who simply don't want to be found.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Logan Fullmer and the Bakers walk through real cases from distressed property deals. They found a deported heir in a Mexican prison in days after the client had searched for months, tracked down a missionary in Uganda, and located a woman in a small town in Peru using a single Facebook account. They also share how they pulled a property from auction with four days to spare, and how a lost-dog flyer during a surveillance job ended up saving a man's life.

Whether you're skip tracing your own leads or deciding when to hire a PI, you'll learn where to look, what it costs, and how to build the sources that break a case open.

You'll learn:
- Why almost nobody is truly a "ghost," and how to find them fast
- How to find someone in jail or federal prison
- How police reports and public records can reveal phone numbers and contacts
- How investigators locate heirs overseas
- What it typically costs to hire a private investigator
- How to use surveillance and pretexts the right way
- How to turn neighbors, local shelters, and libraries into sources
- How to know when to keep digging and when to stop
